title: Home Mortgage Loans: Waiving Late Charges and Other Fees
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Waiving Late Charges and Other Fees

Under Home Mortgage Loans a fee that has been charged can be removed by a waiver, which always cancels the fee in full. There are two reasons a waiver is granted — a bank error or a courtesy — and one limit that applies to every fee.

## Waiver for a bank error

A late charge that the product's late charge rules did not permit — because it should not have been charged at all, or not in the amount charged — is waived, and the waiver is recorded with the reason bank error. This correction is not a courtesy, and it draws nothing from the courtesy allowance described next.

## Courtesy waiver of a late charge

A late charge may be waived as a courtesy while both of the following hold:

- the customer has received fewer courtesy waivers than the program's courtesy allowance, counting every courtesy waiver on any of that customer's mortgage loans during the 365 calendar days that end today; and
- the loan carrying the charge is not in forbearance.

Only waivers recorded as courtesy enter that count. Waivers recorded as bank error are not counted.

## One waiver per fee

Any fee can be waived no more than once. Whether a fee already has a waiver is read from the loan's transaction records, by looking for a waiver entry that points to that same fee.

## Courtesy decision table

| Courtesy waivers for the customer in the last 365 days, compared with the allowance | Loan in forbearance | This fee already waived | Courtesy waiver |
|---|---|---|---|
| fewer | no | no | may be granted |
| fewer | yes | any | not available |
| equal or more | any | any | not available |
| any | any | yes | not available |

## Basis questions

**Does a courtesy waiver granted on one mortgage loan reduce what is left on the customer's other mortgage loans?** Yes. The count covers all of that customer's mortgage loans together.

**When does an old courtesy waiver stop counting?** Once it falls outside the 365 calendar days ending on the current date.

**Hypothetical count.** Take an imagined courtesy allowance of 3. A customer who received courtesy waivers on 10 February and 2 September of last year and on 15 January of this year, is considered on 20 March of this year. The February waiver lies more than 365 days back and no longer counts; the September and January waivers do, so the count is two, below the imagined allowance of 3. The allowance and dates are invented; real allowances are published per program.
